name: Florence Balcombe
bio: Florence Anne Lemon Balcombe, daughter of a retired lieutenant-colonel who had fought in the Crimea, living at 1 Marino Crescent, Clontarf, Dublin. Wilde courted her from August 1876 - he drew her that month and called the courtship 'a memory of two sweet years' - until her engagement in 1878; the editors caption her plate 'Wilde's first love'. She married Bram Stoker on 4 December 1878 at St Anne's Church, Dublin, appeared as a Priestess in Tennyson's The Cup at the Lyceum in January 1881, and remained on cordial terms with Wilde, who sent her Salome in 1893.
bio_note: Born/died (1858-1937), parentage and Clontarf address from the main-particulars footnote at Holland & Hart-Davis, Complete Letters (2000), p. 47 n. 3 (repo PDF 72, folio confirmed, read as page image 2026-08-03), which also records Wilde's August 1876 drawing of her. 'Wilde's first love' from the List of Illustrations, p. vi (repo PDF 6). 'Two sweet years' from Wilde's letter of [? 30 September 1878], p. 71 (repo PDF 98). Stoker marriage from p. 72 n. 1 (repo PDF 99). The Cup casting from p. 107 n. 1 (repo PDF 132). Salome presentation letter at p. 552 (repo PDF 604).
